H1("VII. Legal Points to Note")
B(" FRE 502(d) authorizes a ~federal court~ to order non-waiver binding in other proceedings. The Commission is not a federal court, so the protective order cannot itself be a 502(d) order. Our draft (16(a), 16(e)) eliminates the 502(b) reasonableness inquiry by agreement and commits all parties to jointly seek a true 502(d) order in any 13(b) action and an equivalent ALJ order in Part 3 (we cite 16 C.F.R. § 3.31(g); verify). Given the approximately 1.88 million documents and inherited privilege issues from Whitmore^s 2022–2024 tuck-in acquisitions, this is worth pursuing.", "FRE 502(d).")
B(" Under HSR Act § 7A(h), 15 U.S.C. § 18a(h), Second Request materials are exempt from FOIA and may not be made public except as relevant to an administrative or judicial proceeding; federal–state merger coordination practice generally conditions sharing of HSR materials with state AGs on the parties^ waiver. Our 14(a) language rests on that framework rather than a new notice right. Confirm current agency practice before circulation.", "Para. 14 and state AGs.")
B(" The functional ~competitive decision-making~ test (U.S. Steel Corp. v. United States, 730 F.2d 1465 (Fed. Cir. 1984); Brown Bag Software v. Symantec Corp., 960 F.2d 1465 (9th Cir. 1992)) is the established basis for restricting in-house access and is more defensible than a title- or ~operational responsibility~-based bar. The wall also serves gun-jumping hygiene: until closing, Whitmore and Cascade remain independent competitors (Sherman Act § 1; HSR Act § 7A).", "In-house screen.")
B(" Muñoz pointed to 18 U.S.C. § 1905 and OGE rules. Those protect against unauthorized disclosure by government employees, but 5 C.F.R. § 2635.703 governs current employees and the post-employment statute (18 U.S.C. § 207) restricts representational activity rather than a former economist^s later use of a private party^s commercial data — which supports a narrow departure-notification provision.", "Staff rotation.")
B(" In a Part 3 proceeding the ALJ enters the Commission^s standard protective order under 16 C.F.R. § 3.31(d); in camera treatment is governed by 16 C.F.R. § 3.45. The bridge provision therefore commits the parties to seek supplementation rather than purporting to bind the ALJ (23(b), 23(e)).", "Part 3 interaction.")
B(" Return of materials by the Commission is also governed by 15 U.S.C. § 57b-2 and 16 C.F.R. § 4.12; we should calendar a written return request upon the Conclusion of the Investigation.", "Commission^s own return obligations.")
